record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is P-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism, meaning that applying any homomorphism that never maps a symbol to the empty string to a polynomial-time language always yields another polynomial-time language?

evidence.quote: In [2] this question is reduced to the questions: "IsP-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism ?" and "Is N TIME(n) ~_ P- TIME ?"

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ and $\Gamma$ be finite alphabets. A map $h:\Sigma^*\to\Gamma^*$ is called a homomorphism if $h(uv)=h(u)h(v)$ for all $u,v\in\Sigma^*$, and it is called nonerasing if $h(a)\neq\varepsilon$ for every $a\in\Sigma$. For a language $L\subseteq\Sigma^*$, define $h(L)=\{h(w):w\in L\}\subseteq\Gamma^*$. Let $\mathrm{P}$ denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.

Question: Is $\mathrm{P}$ closed under nonerasing homomorphism? That is, does there hold the implication: for every finite alphabets $\Sigma,\Gamma$, every nonerasing homomorphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Gamma^*$, and every language $L\in\mathrm{P}$ over $\Sigma$, the image $h(L)$ belongs to $\mathrm{P}$?
artifact.status_search_result: It is a standard exercise that P is closed under nonerasing homomorphism if and only if P = NP (equivalently, NTIME(n) ⊆ P implies the closure). Since the P vs NP question remains open, the closure of P under nonerasing homomorphisms is also unresolved.

status_evidence.snippet: Show that P is closed under homomorphism iff P = NP.
status_evidence.claim: Closure of P under nonerasing homomorphism is equivalent to P=NP, hence unresolved.

status_evidence.snippet: P is the class of languages decidable in polynomial time on a deterministic Turing machine; P vs NP is a major open problem.
status_evidence.claim: P vs NP remains open, so the equivalent closure question is open.
